item.title: Your Brain Has a Secret Clock — And It Decides When You Actually Learn
item.description: A Tohoku University study reveals that your brain's capacity for learning fluctuates throughout the day, governed by adenosine and circadian rhythms. Everything you know about 'morning productivity' might be wrong.
item.dc:creator: Cozmic Editorial

item.title: Prozac Doesn't Just Fix Your Mood — It Literally Rewires Your Brain
item.description: A University of Eastern Finland study reveals that fluoxetine works by loosening rigid neural circuits, not just boosting serotonin. The 'chemical imbalance' theory of depression may be fundamentally incomplete.
item.dc:creator: Cozmic Editorial

item.title: Screen Time Before Age 2 Is Silently Reshaping Your Generation's Brain
item.description: A decade-long study links infant screen exposure to accelerated brain maturation, slower decision-making, and teen anxiety. Gen Z was the first generation raised on screens — and the data is finally in.
item.dc:creator: Cozmic Editorial

item.title: Jazz Musicians Are Literally Rewiring Their Brains in Real Time
item.description: A study on jazz pianists reveals that musical improvisation dynamically reconfigures brain networks. Creativity is not a trait — it is a process of continuous neural reorganization.
item.dc:creator: Cozmic Editorial

item.title: Gen Z Is Going Analog — But They're Doing It Wrong
item.description: The generation that grew up online is desperately trying to log off. But posting about being offline on Instagram defeats the purpose. A look at the irony, the science, and the real path forward.
item.dc:creator: Cozmic Editorial

item.title: Gaming Executives Aren't Gamers Anymore — And It's Killing the Industry
item.description: From Xbox's leadership shakeup to the decline of live-service games, the gaming industry is being run by people who do not play games. The consequences are becoming impossible to ignore.
item.dc:creator: Cozmic Editorial

item.title: A 10-Minute Walk Can Rewire Your Memory — Here's the Neuroscience
item.description: You do not need a gym membership to upgrade your brain. A University of Tsukuba study reveals that even light exercise triggers a dopamine and noradrenaline surge in the hippocampus, directly enhancing memory formation.
item.dc:creator: Cozmic Editorial

item.title: How Memories Take Shape at the Synapse Level — Harvard's Breakthrough
item.description: Harvard researchers have developed EPSILON, a revolutionary technique that maps memory formation at the molecular level. The implications for Alzheimer's treatment could be transformative.
item.dc:creator: Cozmic Editorial
